report.summary: All three claims are unfalsifiable; none specifies measurable criteria for 'Gate 0 exits', 'wire through canonical kernel', or 'Gate 1 ignition slice', making them untestable as written.
risks: 11.1 | high | 'Until Gate 0 exits' is unfalsifiable because 'Gate 0' is undefined and no exit criteria are given; the claim cannot be tested or killed without an operational definition. | Define Gate 0 exit criteria and a test that checks whether they have been met.

11.2 | high | 'Wire it through the canonical kernel or keep it as a disposable, isolated experiment' is unfalsifiable because 'canonical kernel' and 'disposable, isolated experiment' are undefined; no test can distinguish compliance from violation. | Define the canonical kernel and the conditions that make an experiment disposable and isolated, then design a test that checks adherence.

11.3 | high | 'The next product proof is the Gate 1 ignition slice, not a broader assistant demo' is unfalsifiable because 'Gate 1 ignition slice' and 'broader assistant demo' are undefined; there is no way to observe which is being built. | Define Gate 1 ignition slice with specific, observable features and define what a broader assistant demo would be, then test which artifact matches.
todos: Define Gate 0 exit criteria with observable, measurable conditions.
Define 'canonical kernel' and 'disposable, isolated experiment' with testable boundaries.
Define 'Gate 1 ignition slice' and 'broader assistant demo' with concrete feature sets so the claim can be falsified.

claims.claim: Until Gate 0 exits, the default answer to new feature work is: wire it through the canonical kernel or keep it as a disposable, isolated experiment.
claims.why: The condition 'Until Gate 0 exits' is undefined. There is no definition of 'Gate 0' nor any criteria that would indicate when it has exited. Without such criteria, no observation can determine whether the condition is true or false, so the claim cannot be tested.

claims.claim: Wire it through the canonical kernel or keep it as a disposable, isolated experiment.
claims.why: The terms 'canonical kernel' and 'disposable, isolated experiment' are not defined. There is no specification of what constitutes the canonical kernel or what makes an experiment disposable and isolated. Without operational definitions, no test can determine whether a given feature is wired correctly or kept as an experiment.

claims.claim: The next product proof is the Gate 1 ignition slice, not a broader assistant demo.
claims.why: 'Gate 1 ignition slice' and 'broader assistant demo' are undefined terms. There is no description of what features or characteristics distinguish a 'Gate 1 ignition slice' from a 'broader assistant demo'. Without such definitions, no observation can determine which one is being built, so the claim cannot be falsified.
